subject: Inference economics alignment: bandwidth, latency tiers, and target $/1M tokens
body:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Lee <sam.lee@novahealth.ai>, Priya Desai <priya.desai@novahealth.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Inference economics alignment: bandwidth, latency tiers, and target $/1M tokens

Hi Sam / Priya —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap + concrete asks so we can model a realistic POC configuration and draft pricing ranges for your finance team. I kept this intentionally short with numbers so Marissa and Vivek can jump in.

Summary of what we heard on the call
- Workload: conversational summaries + document Q&A for clinical intake (mixed short prompts and multi-turn, average context ~1.2k tokens).
- Expected steady-state volume: 8k–12k completions/day; expected peak concurrency ~60 concurrent requests (burst 120).
- Preferred latency SLO: interactive (200–300ms) for triage flows; background/async summarization can tolerate 500–800ms.
- Security: HIPAA-conscious, will require Private or Dedicated with VPC and customer-managed KMS for PII logs.

High-level unit economics (back-of-envelope) — options for target $/1M tokens
Option A — Interactive, streaming-first (SLO ~200–300ms)
- Model: 30B quantized streaming variant on premium tier
- Typical unit cost: ~"$95 per 1M tokens" (includes streaming premium + regional capacity premium)
- Rationale: keeps latency under 300ms; minimal batching; good for triage where response speed is critical

Option B — Mixed SLO, batching for async (SLO 500–800ms for non-critical flows)
- Model: same architecture but allow batching / continuous batching for background jobs
- Typical unit cost: ~"$28–$35 per 1M tokens" when batching 8–16 requests and using quantized runtime
- Rationale: 3x–4x cost reduction at the expense of higher tail latency — good for summarization and bulk processing

Option C — Dedicated reserved capacity (predictable throughput)
- Model: Dedicated pool + autoscale; effective unit cost depends on commit level, but we can structure a band: ~"$40–$70 per 1M tokens" for mid-tier commits (plus monthly reserved fee)
- Rationale: predictable latency and cost; required if you want guaranteed capacity and enhanced network isolation

Marissa / Finance note: if we need to hit a target like "$50/1M tokens" across the board, the architecture usually needs a blend — route interactive traffic to streaming premium and route bulk to batched dedicated nodes with automatic fallback. Expect to trade engineering complexity and a small routing layer for that blended unit cost.

Concrete asks from your side (needed to finalize pricing bands and an estimate CSV):
1) Confirm expected average prompt tokens and average completion tokens (per request). You mentioned ~400 prompt / ~800 completion on the call — can you confirm those numbers per workload (triage vs batch)?
2) Confirm monthly budget band for POC (ballpark is fine): e.g., <$5k, $5–15k, $15–50k, >$50k/month.
3) Any hard latency constraints we must meet for the interactive path (p50/p95 targets)?
4) Are you open to a mixed routing approach (streaming for interactive, batch for async)?

Attachments: I attached a sample CSV schema (novahealth_poc_profile.csv) so we can populate tokens by endpoint, plus a lightweight pricing band chart (redwood_pricing_band_chart.pdf) showing the five example configurations.

Next steps (proposed)
- You: send confirmation on the items above + token profile CSV by EOD Tue 5/4
- Us: we model three POC configurations and send a short pricing worksheet showing unit costs and projected month-1 spend within 48 hours of the CSV
- Optional: 30-minute follow-up to walk Marissa through the unit economics numbers the day we share the worksheet

If it helps, I pasted a tiny worked example below using your mid-case numbers (9k completions/day, avg 1.2k tokens per complete):
- Tokens/day = 9,000 * 1,200 = 10.8M tokens/day -> ~324M tokens/month
- At $95/1M -> ~$30,780/month (streaming SLO)
- At $32/1M -> ~$10,368/month (batched async)

Happy to hop on a quick call to walk through the assumptions.

Thanks —
Karthik Iyer
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Sam Lee <sam.lee@novahealth.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Desai <priya@novahealth.ai>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 15:40:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Inference economics alignment: bandwidth, latency tiers, and target $/1M tokens

Thanks Karthik — this is excellent and very actionable. A few clarifications from our side:
- Average tokens: triage flows ~350 prompt / ~600 completion; bulk summarization ~600 prompt / ~1,400 completion (we often chunk long docs)
- Monthly budget: our initial POC budget is in the $10k–20k/month band (we can stretch a bit for a short pilot)
- Latency: p50 target for interactive is 250ms; p95 should not exceed 550ms ideally (we can tolerate occasional spikes during peak)
- Yes on mixed routing — that model makes sense to us.

We'll upload a quick sample of production logs (sanitized) overnight that has per-request token counts. Priya will coordinate.

Sam
Sam Lee
Head of AI | NovaHealth AI
sam.lee@novahealth.ai | +1 (212) 555-9898

On Fri, Apr 30, 2027 at 16:05:27 -0700, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai> wrote:

Karthik / Team —

Thanks for the clear options. From a finance lens, NovaHealth's $10k–20k/month POC target means we should prioritize a blended approach right away so they can validate latency-sensitive flows without blowing the budget. Two quick notes: 
- Can we show a blended sheet that assumes 40% interactive, 60% batch to model the $/1M target?
- Also include an explicit line for reserved vs on-demand differential so Procurement can see the delta for an initial 3-month commit.

I can prep a short one-page summary for the buyer (Priya) if you drop me the model assumptions in CSV.

Marissa Cole
Director, FinOps Partnerships | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai

> On the cost numbers: to hit a blended $50/1M we typically need at least 50% traffic routed to batched quantized nodes plus a 3-month reserved commit for dedicated capacity. We should call that out explicitly. — Marissa

Great — thanks for the quick confirmations, Sam.

Action items I will take on now:
- Vivek: I’ll loop you to model two concrete POC configs ("Interactive-priority" and "Blended-commit") and produce the CSV with projected monthly spend for the $10k–20k band.
- Marissa: I’ll send a one-page summary called out to Procurement with reserved vs on-demand deltas and the blended $/1M sheet.
- Sam / Priya: please upload the sanitized token log CSV to the Drive link I shared and cc me; I’ll incorporate it into the model.

I attached: redwood_pricing_band_chart.pdf (band-level examples) and novahealth_poc_profile.csv (schema). Expect the worksheet in ~48 hours after we get the CSV. If you'd like a 30-min walkthrough when we send it, let me know 5/3 or 5/4 windows that work.

Karthik
